note: The contract of jidhr's orthographic normaliser. Two implementations read this file: the Go one in jidhr/pkg/root and the Dart one that runs on the device. They must agree exactly — when they drift, recognised speech stops matching text_uthmani and the in-prayer cursor silently never advances — so a change to either starts with a case added here. `remove` and `fold` are complete tables of code points, not a summary: an implementation needs no Unicode database and no access to the Go source to be exactly right. Every input is one token, a word or a fragment copied out of a mushaf, and the format names no language.
algorithm: Iterate the input by Unicode code point. In Dart that is `input.runes`, never `codeUnits`: a mark above U+FFFF is two UTF-16 units, and splitting it leaves two halves of a character that should have been removed whole.
For each code point, in order: if it falls inside any range of `remove`, emit nothing; else if it is a key of `fold`, emit the code point `fold` maps it to; else emit it unchanged.

Concatenate what was emitted. Nothing else happens: no reordering, no Unicode composition or decomposition, no case change, no trimming, no length limit, no lookahead — each code point is decided on its own.
`remove` and `fold` are the contract. Where the prose in `rules` and these two tables disagree, the tables win and the prose is the bug.
scope: Combining marks are removed only inside the Arabic blocks: U+0600..U+06FF Arabic, U+0750..U+077F Arabic Supplement, U+0870..U+089F Arabic Extended-B, U+08A0..U+08FF Arabic Extended-A, U+10EC0..U+10EFF Arabic Extended-C. Arabic Supplement holds no marks today and contributes no ranges.

Arabic Extended-B (U+0870..U+089F) is IN scope. It carries Qur'anic annotation marks, and an implementation that leaves them standing produces a key no other implementation reaches. This is stated because it is the block the two normalisers were most likely to split on.
A combining mark outside those blocks is kept: a Latin combining acute, a Hebrew point, a Devanagari matra all survive untouched.
Invisible formatting characters are removed everywhere, in every block, not only inside the Arabic ones.

The Arabic Presentation Forms (U+FB50..U+FDFF and U+FE70..U+FEFF) are NOT folded to their base letters; only U+FEFF, which is an invisible formatting character rather than a ligature, is removed. See `notUnified`.
The tables below were expanded from Unicode 17.0.0. A future Unicode version adding an Arabic mark is a change to this file, made deliberately with a case, never an implicit change of behaviour.

rules.text: Remove every Arabic combining mark: the short vowels, tanwin, shadda, sukun, the dagger alef and the Qur'anic annotation signs. The exact code points are the `remove` entries whose rule is `marks` — the Unicode Mn characters of the blocks named in `scope`, written out here so that reading this contract needs no Unicode tables.
Remove tatweel (U+0640). It stretches a join for typography and carries no sound.
Map alef with madda (U+0622), alef with hamza above (U+0623), alef with hamza below (U+0625) and alef wasla (U+0671) to a bare alef (U+0627).
Map ta marbuta (U+0629) to ha (U+0647), so a word ends at one key however the writer spelled it.
Map alef maqsura (U+0649) to ya (U+064A), so the dotted and undotted spellings share one key.
Map hamza on a waw seat (U+0624) to waw (U+0648) and hamza on a ya seat (U+0626) to ya (U+064A).
Keep a standalone hamza (U+0621). It is a letter in its own right: دعا and دعاء are different words with different roots.
Remove the Uthmani small waw (U+06E5) and small ya (U+06E6). They lengthen a pronoun vowel and are not letters of the word.

Remove every invisible formatting character: the zero-width non-joiner (U+200C) and joiner (U+200D), the end-of-ayah sign (U+06DD), the byte order mark, the bidi controls and the rest. The exact code points are the `remove` entries whose rule is `invisible` — the Unicode Cf characters, written out here. Unlike the marks these are removed wherever they occur, in any block, because they carry no spelling in any script.
Map the Arabic-Indic digits (U+0660..U+0669) and the extended set a Persian or Urdu keyboard produces (U+06F0..U+06F9) to the Western digits 0..9.

Emit every other code point unchanged, whatever block or script it belongs to. `remove` and `fold` are exhaustive: a code point in neither is copied through, and that includes a combining mark outside the blocks named in `scope`, a Latin letter, a Western digit, a space and any punctuation.

Never remove a prefix, a suffix or the definite article. Normalisation is orthographic only; peeling affixes is the stripping rung's work, and doing it here would fold الفتح into فتح and report the wrong root as a fact.
Normalising a normalised word returns it unchanged. Every `expected` in this file is its own normal form.

cases.why: dagger alef: the superscript alef is a mark, not a letter, and goes with the rest of them
alef wasla: the connecting alef of the definite article becomes a bare alef
hamza seat: alef with hamza above becomes a bare alef
hamza seat: alef with hamza below becomes a bare alef
hamza seat: alef with madda becomes a bare alef
ta marbuta becomes ha, so a word ends at one key however the writer spelled it
ha stays ha, which is what makes it the key the ta marbuta spelling arrives at
alef maqsura becomes ya, so the dotted and undotted spellings share one key
ya stays ya, which is the key the alef maqsura spelling arrives at
tatweel is typographic stretching and carries no sound
hamza on a waw seat becomes its carrier waw
hamza on a ya seat becomes its carrier ya
a standalone hamza is a letter in its own right and survives
the Qur'anic madda sign sits above the letter and is a mark, not a letter
the Uthmani small-high sukun sign is a Qur'anic mark like any other
the small high seen marks a recitation variant and is not part of the spelling
wasla, shadda and dagger alef can land on one word and it must still reduce to one key
modern unvowelled spelling is already normal form, so normalising it again changes nothing
normalisation is orthographic only: an attached waw is a prefix for the stripping rung to peel, not a mark to delete
the Uthmani small high ya lengthens a pronoun vowel and is not a letter, so a word carrying it must still reach the plain key
a hamza written as a combining mark over a bare alef is the same word as one written with the precomposed letter
an invisible non-joiner (U+200C) rides along with copied text and would otherwise make a word match nothing at all
Arabic-Indic digits key the same as the Western ones, so an ayah typed on either keyboard finds the same place
the extended digits a Persian or Urdu keyboard produces key the same as the Arabic-Indic ones
the definite article survives normalisation: peeling it is the stripping rung's work, and folding it here would make الكتاب and كتاب one key
a standalone hamza between two alefs is still a letter, so جاءا does not collapse into جاا
the Uthmani small waw (U+06E5) lengthens a pronoun vowel and is not a letter, so a word carrying it must still reach the plain key
a zero-width joiner (U+200D) rides along with copied text just as the non-joiner does, and neither may survive into a key
the end-of-ayah sign (U+06DD) is invisible and encloses the verse number that follows it, so a verse marker pasted whole still keys as its number
a mark from Arabic Extended-B (U+0898) is in scope and goes with every other mark: this is the block the two implementations would otherwise silently disagree about
a mark above U+FFFF (U+10EFD) is still a mark, and an implementation walking UTF-16 code units rather than code points would keep two broken halves of it
a combining mark outside the Arabic blocks is left alone, so normalising a word of another language never silently rewrites it

selfCheck: For every case: normalising `input` gives `expected`, exactly.
For every case: normalising `expected` gives `expected` — normalising twice must change nothing, or the device and the server disagree the moment either stores a value the other already normalised.
Every `id` in `rules` appears in the `rules` list of at least one case. A rule no case pins is a rule that will drift.
Every rule named by a case exists in `rules`.
No code point is both inside a `remove` range and a key of `fold`.
The `remove` ranges are sorted by `from`, and none overlaps the next.
Run these six against the tables, not against the implementation. A data file that fails loudly beats prose that fails silently.
notUnified: The definite article is NOT removed. It is a prefix for the stripping rung to peel; folding it here would make الفتح and فتح one key and hand back the wrong root as an attested fact.
A standalone hamza (U+0621) is NOT removed or folded. It is a letter: دعا and دعاء are different words with different roots.
No prefix or suffix is removed. وتواصوا normalises to itself; peeling the waw is rung four's work, and doing it here would report a stripped result as an orthographic one.

Folding the seated hamzas is known to merge a few distinct roots — سأل (to ask) reaches the same key as سال (to flow). Accepted: modern typing omits the hamza, so refusing the fold loses far more than it saves, and the exact-spelling rung runs first for any form the corpus actually attests.

The Uthmani spelling ءامنوا does NOT reach the modern آمنوا, and the waw-with-dagger-alef spellings صلوة، زكوة، حيوة do NOT reach صلاة، زكاة، حياة. Both are closed lists of rasm conventions. They are left alone until the corpus exists to measure them, because a wrong fold states a false root where a missing fold only fails to find one.

The Arabic Presentation Forms are NOT folded to their base letters: U+FEFB, the lam-alef ligature, does not reach لا. Neither a keyboard nor a mushaf produces them, so folding them would need a table nothing in the corpus exercises, and an unexercised table is a guess.
